root_cause.text: The error handling path after devm_request_threaded_irq() failure in rockchip_usb2phy_probe() incorrectly jumps to a label that calls of_node_put() on a child node already released by the for_each_available_child_of_node() macro, causing a double decrement of the reference count.
root_cause.evidence: The patch fixes the issue by replacing `goto put_child;` with `return ret;` immediately on irq request failure, avoiding the duplicate `of_node_put()` at the `put_child` label. The CVE description explicitly states that the macro calls `of_node_put()` in each loop iteration and that after breaking from the loop, the `put_child` label would call it again.

Author: Peter Geis <pgwipeout@gmail.com>

    phy: phy-rockchip-inno-usb2: support muxed interrupts

    interrupts.
    Allow the driver to plug in only a single interrupt as necessary.

    Tested-by: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@wolfvision.net>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds a new `devm_request_threaded_irq` call at the end of `rockchip_usb2phy_probe()`, and on failure it jumps to the `put_child` label (line: `goto put_child;`). This label is used elsewhere to call `of_node_put()` on a child node that has already been released by the `for_each_available_child_of_node` macro, causing a double decrement of the reference count. The code does not include any fix to prevent this double put.
